findings.title: Invalid-pattern worker exit misses normal finalization; a manual recovery control exists
observed: Retained startSearch code sets inSearching before worker launch; worker smali puts Pattern.compile within a catch-all range whose exception exit calls A.error(Throwable) without local completion dispatch or flag clearing.
The constructor's message-2 handler restores idle controls via showSearchButton(true); that helper itself does not clear inSearching.
The error overloads perform logging/stack-trace and conditional beta-log persistence, with no explicit search completion dispatch.
initView registers the progress click listener; onClick calls showSearchButton(true) and stopSearch on that control.
inferred: The inspected invalid-pattern path can miss automatic idle restoration after a normal search-button launch.
unknown: Actual malformed-query UI behavior, any global recovery callbacks and timing are untested. No permanent freeze, crash or unrecoverable state is established.

findings.title: PDF backward-only scope excludes the current-page index
observed: Retained worker bytecode uses current page as the exclusive backward-only upper bound, versus an inclusive current-page start for forward-only. New option listeners make those UI choices mutually exclusive.
inferred: Backward-only at page index zero covers no pages; forward-only and backward-only have asymmetric current-page inclusion.
unknown: Intended scope wording and actual directional search results remain unverified. Previous-pages-only semantics could make exclusion intentional.

findings.title: The speech availability helper imposes no maximum string length
observed: For end greater than start, the smali accepts strings longer than one character. A single character additionally excludes the object replacement character and listed punctuation. No maximum-length comparison occurs in this predicate.
inferred: This helper does not provide the previously unresolved upper-length guard before the already-observed truncating queue.
unknown: Complete document-to-queue over-limit reachability still depends on upstream segmentation and transformations. No speech omission has been heard or measured.

findings.title: The selected save bridge propagates a native result to Document.Save
observed: Document.Save() returns save(hand_val), catching Exception and returning false; the historical PDFReader.save wrapper does not consume this boolean.
The selected JNI-export wrapper at 0x15fb40 calls 0x291730 and preserves EAX through cleanup to its return; observed guard-failure exits return zero.
The selected 0x291730 window saves results from direct calls to 0x4ae550 and 0x4afeb0 and restores the selected result after mutex-unlock handling.
inferred: The result-producing calls at 0x4ae550 and 0x4afeb0 are specific next inspection boundaries for native save semantics.
unknown: Those downstream implementations, previous-xref state, actual return values during the form experiment and exact SDK version remain unknown. This does not identify the cause of /Prev -1 or prove the ignored boolean caused malformed output.

findings.title: The selected saveAs wrapper sets its success byte after its helper returns
observed: On the observed file-open-success route the wrapper calls 0x15fe70, performs cleanup and sets BPL to 1 at 0x15fd6c without testing the helper's EAX. The final mov eax,ebp carries AL=1, not necessarily full-width EAX=1.
inferred: This route motivates checking save-as completion and durable output together if the workflow is reachable.
unknown: The helper's return type, result semantics and failure handling are not established. The bounded helper window contains setup only. No discarded boolean failure or association with the recorded close-triggered saves is proved.
